newsitem.title: USA: Chips & Tech sees FY 97 EPS of $1.10-1.25.
newsitem.headline: Chips & Tech sees FY 97 EPS of $1.10-1.25.

text.p: Chips and Technologies Inc chief financial officer Tim Christoffersen said that he is comfortable with the range of estimates on Wall Street for fiscal 1997 of $1.10-$1.25 a share on a fully taxed basis.

Christoffersen, who earlier Thursday addressed a Salomon Brothers Technology Conference here, said in a phone interview that there was nothing new in his presentation at the Salomon conference and he could only attribute the rise in the company's stock to a sympathy move with Intel Corp.
Shares of Chips and Technologies were up 4-1/8 to 23-7/8 in very active trading. Intel was up 4-3/8 to 123-3/8.

Chips and Technologies, based in San Jose, Calif., develops semiconductors for use in personal computers and notebook computers. It recently signed a deal with Lockheed Martin Corp to develop two-dimensional, three-dimensional and video graphics controller chips.
Intel Corp, which gave a bullish projection for the fourth quarter late Wednesday, will be incorporating these graphics chips developed with Lockheed into a new PC platform card.
"We have been getting a lot of interest and attention from our partnership with Lockheed-Martin," Christoffersen said. "Maybe that puts us in a favorable light along with Intel."
Christoffersen said that Intel plans to roll out its add-in cards with the graphics accelerators chips in 1997.

Chips and Technologies said its fiscal 1997 ends in June and that it is better to talk about earnings on a fully-taxed basis for next year. That's because this year, the company is at a 10 percent tax rate while it still sees some tax benefits from its previous losses.
"Fully taxed numbers are the ones to look at," Christoffersen said.
At the company's current tax rate of about 10 percent, Christoffersen said, the analysts' estimates are in the range of $1.50 to $1.75 a share, for fiscal 1997.
